title: What defines a team’s success in Major League Baseball
text:
Lincoln, NE- We are often told in baseball that hitting home runs is one of the leading factors that leads to a team’s success in Major League Baseball.
I wanted to look at the following three categories of stats, team home-runs, stolen bases, and on base percentage from the 2021 to 2024 seasons.
But, in my project I will be showing that it is more than just home-runs that defines what contributes to a team’s success.
Let’s take a look at some numbers, mlb_hitter_value_2014_2024. I decided to take a look at hitting stats from the 2021 season to the 2024 season.
The first question I want to ask is, what was the average, based on the team home run totals for the 2021 season.
The average amount of home runs for the 2021 season was 187.3333.


Code
library(baseballr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

hitterstats <- read_csv("data/mlb_hitter_stats_1914_2024(in).csv")

# 1. Load, filter (2021 and above), and select core variables from historical data
historical_filtered <- read_csv("data/mlb_hitter_stats_1914_2024(in).csv") %>%
  filter(Season >= 2021)

teamtotals <- historical_filtered |> 
  filter(grepl("TM", Team) == FALSE) |> 
  group_by(Team, Season) |> 
  summarize(
    total_hr = sum(HR),
    avg_war = mean(WAR, na.rm=TRUE),
    
  )

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(
    data=teamtotals,
    aes(
      x=Season,
      y=total_hr,
      group=Team
    )
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 187.3333, color="blue") + 
  facet_wrap(~Team)











Code
teamtotals <- hitterstats |>
  filter(between(Season, 2021, 2024)) |>
  filter(!grepl("TM", Team)) |>
  group_by(Team, Season) |>
  summarise(
    total_hr = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(Team)

ggplot(teamtotals, aes(x = total_hr, y = reorder(Team, total_hr))) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = total_hr),
    size = 2.5,
    direction = "y"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Season, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "MLB Team Home Run Totals (2021–2024)",
    subtitle = "Teams organized by home run production",
    x = "Total Home Runs",
    y = "MLB Team"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









For my second chart, I decided to look at a facet wrap of all MLB team home runs by home run production from the 2021 season to the 2024 season.


Code
hitterstats <- read_csv("data/mlb_hitter_stats_1914_2024(in).csv")

team_war <- hitterstats |>
  filter(between(Season, 2021, 2024)) |>
  filter(!is.na(WAR)) |>
  group_by(Team) |>
  summarise(
    Average_WAR = mean(WAR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(Team) |>
  mutate(Team = factor(Team, levels = Team))

# Filter and clean data
war_data <- hitterstats |>
  filter(between(Season, 2021, 2024)) |>
  filter(!is.na(WAR), !is.na(Player)) |>
  filter(!grepl("TM", Team))

# Calculate average WAR
avg_war <- mean(war_data$WAR, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create scatterplot
ggplot(war_data, aes(x = Season, y = WAR)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = war_data |> filter(WAR >= 5),
    aes(label = Player),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = avg_war,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2021,
    y = avg_war,
    label = paste("Average WAR:", round(avg_war, 2)),
    color = "red",
    vjust = -0.8,
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2021:2024) +
  labs(
    title = "MLB Player WAR (2021–2024)",
    subtitle = "Individual hitter performance compared to average WAR",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Wins Above Replacement (WAR)",
    caption = "Source: MLB Hitter Statistics (1914–2024) | Data: baseballr | Created by: Mark Borseth"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









For my third chart, I’m looking at individual hitter performance that is compared to the average wins above replacement for the 2021 season to the 2024 season. In other words, looking at the top ten hitters in those three seasons.


Code
# Select top 10 players in each season
top_players <- war_data |>
  group_by(Season) |>
  slice_max(WAR, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

# Create scatterplot
ggplot(war_data, aes(x = Season, y = WAR)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.4,
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = top_players,
    aes(label = Player),
    size = 3,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.4,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = mean(war_data$WAR, na.rm = TRUE),
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2021:2024) +
  labs(
    title = "MLB Player WAR (2021–2024)",
    subtitle = "Top 10 hitters labeled in each season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Wins Above Replacement (WAR)",
    caption = "Source: MLB Hitter Statistics (1914–2024) | Data: baseballr | Created by: Mark Borseth"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









For my last chart, I will be talking about the top 10 MLB teams by on base percentage on average from 2021 to 2024.


Code
team_obp <- hitterstats |>
  filter(between(Season, 2021, 2024)) |>
  filter(!is.na(OBP), !grepl("TM", Team)) |>
  group_by(Team) |>
  summarise(
    Average_OBP = mean(OBP, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Average_OBP)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

ggplot(team_obp, aes(x = reorder(Team, Average_OBP),
                     y = Average_OBP)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(Average_OBP, 3)),
    hjust = -0.2,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 MLB Teams by On-Base Percentage",
    subtitle = "Average OBP from 2021–2024",
    x = "MLB Team",
    y = "Average On-Base Percentage",
    caption = "Source: MLB Hitter Statistics (1914–2024) | Data: baseballr | Created by:Mark Borseth"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  expand_limits(y = max(team_obp$Average_OBP) * 1.08)









It turns out, that there is much more to a team’s individual success in Major League Baseball than what you normally think about when it comes to success in the major leagues.
